text:
maya: quick heads-up — after switching the llama3-13b -> llm.int8 (bitsandbytes) default bundle in staging, we see a noticeable perf win but a quality dip on a subset of sparse-activation prompts (docs with lots of bullet lists / code snippets). anyone else?

arjun: saw the dashboard, curious how big the delta is. numbers? :thinking_face:

maya: baseline fp16 eval (internal devset slice): 92.4% exact-match. llm.int8 run: 90.1%. overall MMLU/afew-other benchmarks are flat but the sparse slice drops ~2.3 EM.

samir: that's larger than expected. throughput/latency tradeoffs at least?

maya: throughput +28% tokens/s and median latency down 18ms on p4dn configs. so perf is solid.

jess: do we have logits/top-k differences on those failing examples? could be top-1 probability shifts from quant noise.

maya: yes — grabbed softmax deltas for a few examples. on some tokens the top-prob shifts 0.12 -> 0.08 which pushes a different token. here's one sample diff: 
```
input: "- install dependencies:
  - python>=3.10
  - libX"
fp16 top3: [("python",0.38),("pip",0.12),("python3",0.05)]
int8 top3: [("pip",0.35),("python",0.15),("python3",0.04)]
```

arjun: interesting — looks like a swap between high-prob tokens, not total collapse. could be bucketized outlier weights in certain feedforward views. did llm.int8 use norm folding/adaquant options?

maya: we used llm.int8 default from our bundle: enable_8bit=True, use_double_quant=True, quant_type="nf4". no per-layer overrides.

samir: can you repro with bitsandbytes standalone? try with use_double_quant=False and with int8-ColD fallback for first 4 layers.

maya: running that now. also running a narrow eval that isolates list/code-style prompts (~800 examples). will post results.

(30s later)

maya: quick update — disabling double-quant reduced the delta to ~1.1 EM on the slice. enabling fp16 fallback for the first 6 transformer blocks removes almost all regression (0.2 EM).

jess: that suggests a small set of layers are sensitive. we could add a fast auto-detect: run a calibration pass on a small prompt sample, measure KL per-layer, and mark layers with KL>threshold to run in fp16.

arjun: agree. keep in mind perf hit for fp16 layers is primarily memory + KV cache behavior. but if it's just first 6 layers the throughput drop is small (~6% in our baseline). worth it for quality.

samir: can we do a hybrid profile: llm.int8 with a per-model profile mapping (e.g., fallback_layers=[0,1,2,3,4,5]) integrated into the bundle metadata? then rollout can still be 100% but with safety.

maya: i like that. i'll prototype a profile format and a tiny calibration job that we run during model onboard. will include a small prompt set (50 examples) sampled from docs/code slices.

ci-bot: perf/regression job 1837004821-llmint8-run completed — throughput: +27%, median latency: -18ms, sparse-slice EM delta: -2.3 -> -0.2 after applying dynamic-fallback profile.

jess: nice. what's the plan for canary?

maya: propose: 5% canary with profile off (to measure real-world regression), 5% canary with dynamic-fallback profile on, compare metrics over 24h. auto-revert rule: >1.0 EM regression on critical eval slice or error-rate >0.5%.

arjun: add an alert if KL-per-token spikes >0.15 for any route. also log per-request quantation-mode tag for traceability.

samir: also test extreme temps/creative prompts — quant noise sometimes amplifies with high temp. run temp sweep (0.2, 0.7, 1.2) on the failing slice.

maya: doing temp sweep; early result: at temp=1.2 regression increases by ~0.6 EM. will include in rollout risk doc.

jess: ok. once we have profile format and small calibrator, let's add to model onboarding checklist: run llm.int8 cal job, store profile in model catalog, attach profile to default bundle.

maya: will PR the calibrator and a sample profile. pinging @arjun and @samir for review when ready.

arjun: can help with perf microbenchmarks for fp16-fallback cost.

samir: I'll run extended evals against SQuAD, CodeAlly, and our docs set overnight.

maya: thanks — will follow up with results + PR link. :thumbsup:
